title: Explode / How it’s made
note: Educational assembly order · H-10 internals approximate · Not a factory assembly guide

closing.title: A movement becomes a watch.
closing.description: Stored energy, a steady rhythm, a readable display and a protective case. Every layer now has a place—and a reason to be here.

chapters.title: Begin with stored energy.
chapters.description: Winding bends a coiled metal ribbon, storing elastic energy. As the mainspring unwinds, it supplies the watch’s power. This is the energy store; the smaller hairspring we meet later controls rhythm.
chapters.joined: The spring is our starting point. Next, give it a drum that can deliver its energy.
chapters.detail: Mainspring · Illustrative ribbon geometry; alloy and dimensions unverified

chapters.title: Give the spring a home.
chapters.description: The barrel surrounds the mainspring. Its toothed rim passes power into the wheel train. Watch it enclose the spring you just explored: the hidden part still belongs to the working assembly.
chapters.joined: The spring and barrel now form the energy supply. Add the gears that carry its output.
chapters.detail: Barrel and arbor · Hidden H-10 geometry approximate

chapters.title: Carry energy through the gears.
chapters.description: Meshing wheels pass torque from the barrel toward the escapement and display. Different wheel sizes establish different rates of rotation. Their exact tooth counts and placement here are illustrative.
chapters.joined: The energy now has a path. Without regulation, it would run down too quickly.
chapters.detail: Wheel train · Power transmission; not a calibrated gear simulation

chapters.title: Release it a little at a time.
chapters.description: The escapement alternately locks and releases the escape wheel. It also gives impulses to the balance, linking the gear train’s energy to the oscillator that controls the pace.
chapters.joined: The release mechanism is in place. It needs a regular rhythm to follow.
chapters.detail: Escapement · General operating principle; H-10 geometry approximate

chapters.title: Give the mechanism a rhythm.
chapters.description: The balance wheel swings back and forth as its fine hairspring supplies a restoring force. Together they regulate the escapement. This hairspring sets the rhythm; the mainspring stores the power.
chapters.joined: Power and regulation now work together. Their pivots still need a supporting structure.
chapters.detail: Balance wheel and hairspring · Motion illustrates the principle, not calibrated timing

chapters.title: Hold the working parts in alignment.
chapters.description: The mainplate and bridges locate the moving parts. Jewel bearings support pivots while separate bridges secure the mechanism. These supports conceal some gears when seated, but do not remove them.
chapters.joined: The mechanism has its supports. Next, add the route that replenishes the spring.
chapters.detail: Support plates and bridges · Reference-informed visible forms; hidden details approximate

chapters.title: Connect motion to winding.
chapters.description: The automatic winding train transfers rotor motion toward the mainspring. Its wheels make a connection between movement of the watch and the stored energy that drives timekeeping.
chapters.joined: The winding path is in place. Add the weight that responds to your wrist.
chapters.detail: Winding train · Exact reversing arrangement and ratios unverified

chapters.title: Let your wrist supply the energy.
chapters.description: The weighted rotor swings around its bearing as the watch moves. Beneath it, the winding train replenishes the mainspring. Its openings let you glimpse the mechanism it serves.
chapters.joined: The rotor joins the winding train. Pause here to see how these parts form a complete automatic movement.

chapters.title: The H-10 movement.
chapters.description: The parts now form one system: the rotor and winding train replenish the mainspring; the barrel and gears transmit its energy; the escapement and balance regulate its release. Plates and bridges hold that chain together.
chapters.joined: Stored energy now becomes regulated motion. Build the dial and hands onto this movement to make time readable.
chapters.detail: Milestone · Automatic movement · Educational assembly order

chapters.title: Turn motion into something readable.
chapters.description: The matte dial gives time a fixed scale: hour numerals and fine minute divisions. It stays still while the hands move above it.
chapters.joined: The scale is in place. Add the pointers that make it useful.

chapters.title: Give time its pointers.
chapters.description: Three hands share a center at different heights. The cathedral outlines frame luminous inserts; the hour, minute and seconds hands make different timescales visible.
chapters.joined: The mechanism now has a readable face. It still needs protection.

chapters.title: Build a home around it.
chapters.description: The steel case surrounds the movement and display. Its openings and supports connect the internal assembly to the crown, windows and strap.
chapters.joined: The case brings the layers into one object. Now connect the controls.

chapters.title: Put control within reach.
chapters.description: The crown provides the wearer’s connection to setting and winding. Its gripped edge makes a small mechanical control usable by hand.
chapters.joined: The control joins the case. Next, attend to its boundaries.

chapters.title: Pay attention to the joins.
chapters.description: Gaskets belong at interfaces between case parts. Their placement matters as much as the visible metal; this illustrative model does not establish actual sealing performance.
chapters.joined: The interfaces are represented. Close the back while keeping the mechanism visible.

chapters.title: Frame a view from behind.
chapters.description: The metal caseback ring retains the rear window and closes around the movement. The back is an assembly with its own structure, not a painted surface.
chapters.joined: The retaining ring is in place. Its opening still needs a window.

chapters.title: Keep the mechanism in view.
chapters.description: The transparent rear window lets you see the rotor beneath it. Its material composition is unverified in our references, so we do not label it sapphire.
chapters.joined: The rear is closed and still transparent. Protect the display on the other side.

chapters.title: Protect the face without hiding it.
chapters.description: The front sapphire sits above the hands. Its curved edge and moving reflections reveal a clear protective surface while preserving the view of the dial.
chapters.joined: The display is protected. One last connection makes the watch wearable.

chapters.title: Bring it back to the wrist.
chapters.description: The leather strap connects the case to the wearer. That closes the story: the wrist carries the watch, and its motion helps wind the mechanism inside.
chapters.joined: The layers have become one watch. Scroll a little farther to see it together.

opening.title: A whole world on your wrist.
opening.description: Start with the complete Murph. Scroll into its mainspring, explore each working part, then build the movement and the watch around it.
